title: Additivity of complexity under product with a deterministic protocol
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a shared-randomness space and let $X$, $Y$ be private input sets. Let $p_1$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over $\Omega$, $X$, $Y$ with output type $\alpha_1$, and let $p_2$ be a deterministic finite-message protocol over $X$, $Y$ with output type $\alpha_2$. Form their product: the public-coin protocol over $\Omega$, $X$, $Y$ with output type $\alpha_1 \times \alpha_2$ that runs both $p_1$ and $p_2$ on the same inputs, sharing the randomness $\Omega$, and returns the pair of their outputs. Then the worst-case communication complexity of this product protocol equals the sum of the complexities of $p_1$ and $p_2$.
hypotheses_covered: p_1 is a public-coin finite-message protocol over Ω, X, Y with output α₁
p_2 is a deterministic finite-message protocol over X, Y with output α₂
replaced:
The complexity of $\mathrm{prodDet}\;p_1\;p_2$ equals the sum of the complexity of $p_1$
and the complexity of $p_2$:
$(\mathrm{prodDet}\;p_1\;p_2).\mathrm{complexity} =
  p_1.\mathrm{complexity} + p_2.\mathrm{complexity}$.
